sanskrit_verse: अव्यायच्छन्न अविक्रोशन् स्वामिने चानिवेदयन् । वोढुमर्हति गोपस्तां विनयं चैव राजनि ॥
transliteration: avyāyacchann avikrośan svāmine cānivedayan | voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ caiva rājani ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who conceals a crime without protest or report to the sovereign, that guardian bears the burden of rectification and must restore order under royal authority.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the Sovereign as representative of Dharma
Concealment constitutes a causal obstruction to justice
Capacity-based responsibility extends to all witnesses and guardians
Restoration logic demands active correction of concealed harm
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual possesses knowledge of a transgression AND fails to disclose it to lawful authority THEN that individual assumes proportional restorative obligation
IF concealment results in systemic imbalance THEN the concealer is assigned completion-process duties until equilibrium is restored
IF a custodian or witness engages in silence THEN capacity for future testimony is suspended until integrity is re-established
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Adjudication, any act of concealment by a custodian or witness invokes automatic restorative liability. The threshold of responsibility includes omission. The court must ensure alignment with Dharma through corrective assignment rather than punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that unspoken knowledge disrupts causal flow. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how silence distorts sequential dharma. Proportional responsibility lies in restoring what was hidden. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that concealment is not punished but corrected via conscious reintegration.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Truth-Revelation Process wherein the concealer is guided to voluntarily disclose suppressed data
Assign Correctional Service aligned with the nature of the concealed act to restore systemic balance
Enforce Witness Integrity Reconditioning to rehabilitate capacity for dharmic testimony
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: Concealment yields not punishment but correction; Dharma is restored through conscious alignment; Reality remains non-punitive; Consciousness alone is the final adjudicator.
